plants.name: Monstera

water.method: Water slowly until it runs from the drainage holes, then empty the saucer. Let the top 2-3 inches of soil dry before watering again.

plants.sun: Bright indirect light; keep out of direct midday sun, which can scorch the leaves
plants.soil: Chunky, well-draining aroid mix (bark, perlite, potting soil)
plants.fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer monthly, spring through summer; skip in winter
plants.humidity: 40-60% — mist occasionally or run a humidifier nearby
plants.temperature: 65-85°F, away from cold drafts and AC vents
plants.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed (calcium oxalate crystals)
plants.healthySigns: Firm, glossy deep-green leaves with open fenestrations (splits); steady new growth
plants.warningSigns: Yellow leaves = overwatered, let it dry out more. Crispy brown edges = underwatered or humidity too low. Drooping = thirsty, water soon.
plants.notes: One leaf already has minor brown-tipped damage in the photo — not urgent, just keep an eye on it. Rotate the pot occasionally for even growth. Last-watered date not yet recorded — log it in the app once known so the schedule is accurate.

plants.name: Mixed Planter (Bird of Paradise + Mandevilla)
plants.species: Strelitzia sp. (Bird of Paradise) + Mandevilla sp., combo planter

water.method: Water thoroughly until it drains; let the top 1-2 inches of soil dry before watering again

plants.sun: Full sun to bright indirect — the Mandevilla blooms best with 4-6+ hours of direct sun
plants.soil: Well-draining potting mix with added perlite/organic matter
plants.fertilizer: Balanced fertilizer every 2-4 weeks, spring through summer; skip in winter
plants.humidity: Moderate to high — both plants appreciate occasional misting
plants.temperature: 65-85°F; the Mandevilla is frost-tender, bring it in below 50°F
plants.toxicity: Mandevilla sap can irritate skin/eyes and is toxic if ingested; Bird of Paradise seeds/fruit are toxic to pets
plants.healthySigns: Upright glossy Bird of Paradise leaves; Mandevilla producing white blooms and healthy new vine growth
plants.warningSigns: Yellowing or dropping leaves = overwatered. Wilting or crispy leaves = underwatered. Few or no blooms = not enough light.
plants.notes: Best-guess ID from photo — this is a mixed nursery planter with at least two different plants sharing one pot (a Bird-of-Paradise-type upright plant and a flowering Mandevilla vine). They share soil, so water on this schedule but watch each one separately for stress signs. Last-watered date not yet recorded — log it in the app once known.

plants.name: Moth Orchid

water.amountText: about 3 ice cubes, or a light soak
water.method: Water when the bark is dry and roots look silvery rather than green. Soak and let fully drain — never let the roots or crown sit in water, and never water directly into the crown (center).

plants.sun: Bright, indirect light — an east-facing window is ideal. Direct sun can scorch the leaves.
plants.soil: Orchid bark mix — NOT regular potting soil. Must drain very freely.
plants.fertilizer: Weak balanced orchid fertilizer (quarter strength) every 2 weeks while actively growing; skip while blooming
plants.humidity: 50-80% — use a pebble tray or humidifier, since typical home humidity is usually too low
plants.temperature: 65-80°F daytime; a ~10°F nighttime drop can help trigger reblooming
plants.healthySigns: Firm green-silver roots, thick unwrinkled leaves, long-lasting blooms
plants.warningSigns: Mushy black roots or crown = overwatered (crown rot — serious, can kill the plant). Shriveled leaves or dry silvery roots = underwatered. A few yellow leaves at the very bottom can be a normal, harmless cycle.
plants.notes: Currently in full bloom. Last-watered date not yet recorded — log it in the app once known so the schedule is accurate.

plants.name: Mandevilla (balcony trellis)

water.method: Water deeply until it drains; check the top 1-2 inches of soil and water when dry. Outdoor containers dry out faster in sun and wind — check more often than an indoor plant.

plants.sun: Full sun — at least 4-6 hours of direct sun daily for best blooming
plants.fertilizer: Balanced or bloom-boosting fertilizer every 2-4 weeks, spring through summer
plants.temperature: Thrives 65-85°F; bring indoors once nights drop below 50°F
plants.toxicity: Sap can irritate skin and eyes; toxic if ingested by pets or people
plants.healthySigns: Glossy deep-green leaves, healthy vine growth, regular new buds and blooms
plants.warningSigns: Yellow leaves or leaf drop = overwatered. Wilting or crispy leaves = underwatered, or too much sun without enough water.
plants.notes: Container-grown on a trellis, outdoors on the balcony — check soil moisture more often than an indoor plant, especially in hot or windy weather. Bring it indoors before the first frost, once nights are below 50°F. Last-watered date not yet recorded — log it in the app once known.

plants.name: Pothos (hanging basket)
plants.species: Epipremnum aureum (Pothos) or Philodendron hederaceum — very similar care either way

water.method: Water thoroughly until it drains, then let the top 1-2 inches of soil dry out before watering again — check by feel, not by calendar.

plants.sun: Bright indirect light; tolerates medium/low light but grows more slowly
plants.fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer monthly, spring through summer; skip in winter
plants.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed
plants.healthySigns: Firm, glossy green leaves and active new vine growth
plants.warningSigns: Yellow leaves are usually from OVERWATERING (the most common cause) — let the soil dry out more before watering again, rather than watering more. Crispy brown leaves = underwatered or humidity too low.
plants.notes: ⚠️ Currently showing yellowing leaves in the photo. The most likely cause is overwatering (roots sitting in wet soil), not too little water — let the soil dry out more than usual before the next watering, confirm the basket/pot actually drains, and trim off any fully yellowed leaves.
